best_for: Makers, students and small workshops who draw 2D plans and parts in DXF and do not want to pay for an AutoCAD license.

points.title: 2D only
points.text: LibreCAD is a 2D drafting tool. There is no 3D modeling, so it fits floor plans, laser-cut outlines and mechanical drawings, not solid parts.

points.title: DXF first, DWG in some builds
points.text: It reads and writes DXF from R12 up to R2018, and exports PDF and SVG. DWG import and export work only in builds compiled with DWG support, so test a sample file before you rely on it.

points.title: Free with no strings
points.text: LibreCAD is free software under the GPL v2, with no trials, subscriptions or license fees, and it is translated into more than 30 languages.

points.title: Mac builds lag a little
points.text: The macOS listing here is at 2.2.1.5 while Windows and Linux are at 2.2.1.6. Homebrew disabled its LibreCAD cask in September 2026 because the app failed Apple's Gatekeeper check, so Mac users install from the project's own .dmg.

points.title: Windows still has 32-bit
points.text: Both 32-bit and 64-bit Windows installers are offered, and both install machine-wide, which helps on older shop PCs.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 11 versions. macOS (separate Intel and Apple Silicon builds) and Linux list only the current release. The Flatpak is verified on Flathub, and the project also offers AppImage and Snap builds on GitHub.
